findings.claim: docs/gates/** is absent from CODEOWNERS. The USER-GATE-D Threshold A sign-off artefact (the gate that closes WP-SCP-023) has no code owner. In multi-maintainer mode, any contributor can modify or pre-fill the operator signature stub and merge it without @jrnb2024 review, falsely advancing WP-SCP-023 to closed.
findings.evidence: CODEOWNERS covers docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/security/**, docs/adoption/**, docs/plans/**, docs/integrations/**, docs/scorecards/**, docs/releases/** — but no rule covers docs/gates/** or docs/reviews/**. Grep of CODEOWNERS for 'docs/gates' and 'docs/reviews' returns no matches. USER-GATE-D was added in this slice at docs/gates/USER-GATE-D.md (line 3: 'not-yet-signed') with no accompanying CODEOWNERS addition. CODEOWNERS line 27: 'In single-operator count=0 mode the rule is documentary; in multi-maintainer mode it is machine-enforced.' The 2026-07-21 bus-factor-1 escalation review is the planned inflection point; the CODEOWNERS gap will become exploitable from that date unless closed first.
findings.impact: After a second maintainer is added post 2026-07-21, any contributor can open a PR modifying docs/gates/USER-GATE-D.md to fill in the date and 'Signed: <attacker>' fields. Without CODEOWNERS routing this to @jrnb2024, the PR can be merged by any maintainer with write access. The false sign-off triggers STATUS.md close, memory updates, and the WP-SCP-023 governance record showing closed — all without the real operator's consent. The ORDERING INVARIANT commentary in CODEOWNERS documents that governance-sensitive paths must be explicitly covered; USER-GATE-D is as governance-sensitive as DECISIONS.md.
findings.mitigation: Add 'docs/gates/** @jrnb2024' to CODEOWNERS before the /CODEOWNERS self-protection line (per ORDERING INVARIANT at line 27). Also consider 'docs/reviews/** @jrnb2024' for the same reason — review dispatch packages carry the audit trail. Both additions should land in this PR or before the 2026-07-21 bus-factor-1 review at the absolute latest.

findings.claim: _resolve_audit_key_id's except clause catches (ValueError, OSError, AttributeError) but does not cover IndexError or RuntimeError. project_root() is implemented as Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] — .parents[2] can raise IndexError if the resolved path has fewer than 3 components, and a future refactor of project_root() could introduce other exception types. The 'NEVER blocks a tool call' invariant is not formally unconditional.
findings.evidence: tools.py lines 433-444: 'except (ValueError, OSError, AttributeError): return "key-ring-unreadable"'. resources.py line 9: 'return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]'. Path.resolve() raises OSError (caught). .parents[2] raises IndexError if len(parents) < 3 (not caught). IndexError is impossible in a correctly installed package but absent from the except clause. Additionally _current_signing_key_id's dict comprehension at lines 924-928 uses 'token.split("=", 1)[1]' guarded by 'if "=" in token' — safe — but the guard itself could be bypassed by a pathological token containing '=' as only the last character, producing an empty string for key rather than raising. No IndexError risk from there. The formal gap is .parents[2].
findings.impact: In a pathologically degraded environment (e.g., the package installed at a root-level path with < 3 components, which is functionally impossible under pip/uv), IndexError propagates through _log_tool_invocation and blocks every tool call. More practically, the absence of 'except Exception' means a future refactor of project_root() that introduces RuntimeError would silently break the fallback guarantee without a test catching it. Severity MIN: IndexError is impossible in any realistic deployment; the risk is forward-looking.
findings.mitigation: Widen to 'except Exception' and add an observability log line: TOOL_LOGGER.warning("_resolve_audit_key_id fallback triggered: %s", repr(exc)). This formally guarantees the invariant regardless of future project_root() changes and preserves observability. One-line change; the sentinel value and overall design are correct.

findings.claim: Audit attribution is fully degraded in the current operational state. docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub contains only comments — no key entries — so every tool invocation logs key_id=key-ring-unreadable. USER-GATE-D criterion (vi) gates the TF-023D-003 code change (complete) but does not gate actual key provisioning. No blocking criterion enforces key generation before Threshold A sign-off.
findings.evidence: docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub (6 lines): header comment only, zero 'ssh-ed25519 ...' entries. _current_signing_key_id (tools.py lines 905-936) iterates key ring lines matching _SIGNING_KEY_LINE_PATTERN looking for current=true; with no entries, raises ValueError at line 932. _resolve_audit_key_id catches this and returns 'key-ring-unreadable'. _log_tool_invocation logs: 'key_id=key-ring-unreadable' for every tool call. USER-GATE-D criterion (vi): 'TF-023D-003 closed. _log_tool_invocation reads the active key_id from docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub' — the code change is done; the pub file has no active key to return. DISPATCH-NOTE Risk 2 acknowledges the degradation but calls it a mitigation ('fallback to key-ring-unreadable'), not a gate.
findings.impact: Until the operator runs 'scp-mcp-server keygen' and commits the public key to the pub file, audit logs cannot attribute tool invocations to an operator key. In a forensic review, key_id=key-ring-unreadable provides no attribution. Additionally propose() is blocked until a key is provisioned (propose_impl raises SCP-MCP-E021 on ValueError from _current_signing_key_id — no fallback in the propose path). The impact is bounded: propose() blockage is by design; audit degradation is acknowledged. The gap is that USER-GATE-D could be signed with criterion (vi) checked while logs remain unattributed.
findings.mitigation: Add a distinct criterion to USER-GATE-D: '(vi-b) Key provisioned. docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub contains at least one entry with current=true and key_id present. Verify by running scp-mcp-server keygen and confirming TOOL_LOGGER output shows key_id != key-ring-unreadable.' This separates the code change (closeable now) from the operational pre-condition (requires offline keygen step). Include the keygen command in the post-signoff actions or add it to STATUS.md as a tracked follow-up gated on Threshold A criteria.

findings.claim: TF-023A-002 (cross-repo notification to ACC / CT / mapp-estate-regression) is listed as IN scope in DISPATCH-NOTE but has not been delivered. ~/Projects/control-tower/governance/docs/notifications/ contains no new files. Estate adopters who need to coordinate opt-in have received no announcement.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md lines 34-35 (scope-IN table): 'Cross-repo notification to ACC / CT / mapp-estate-regression (TF-023A-002 closure) — append a note to ~/Projects/control-tower/governance/docs/notifications/ per reference_ct_notifications.md'. Glob of ~/Projects/control-tower/governance/docs/notifications/** returned no files (directory appears absent or empty). The current branch HEAD 2883087 has three untracked files in docs/reviews/WP-SCP-023/dispatches/023E-threshold/ but no notification file in the control-tower path. USER-GATE-D criterion (vii): 'Cross-repo notification sent. ~/Projects/control-tower/governance/docs/notifications/ carries the v1.2.0 + scorecards announcement.' — this criterion is false.
findings.impact: Without the announcement, CT / ACC / mapp-estate-regression operators are not informed that v1.2.0 + scorecard-emit is available for opt-in. No real adopter can proactively opt in. USER-GATE-D criterion (vii) blocks Threshold A sign-off until delivered, so the gate correctly prevents false closure. The impact is delay to WP-SCP-023 closure rather than a security bypass. Severity MIN because the gate captures it; the finding is that the scope decision was recorded as IN but not executed.
findings.mitigation: Deliver the cross-repo notification before or immediately after PR merge. If the operator decides to defer it past this PR, move TF-023A-002 explicitly from 'scope-IN' to 'scope-OUT-tracked-forward' in DISPATCH-NOTE or STATUS.md with a clear blocking marker on USER-GATE-D criterion (vii). The memory entry reference_ct_notifications.md documents the notification format and path.

findings.claim: USER-GATE-D criterion (vi) is ambiguous between the code change (done) and the operational state (not done). An operator could mark criterion (vi) checked after verifying tools.py while _log_tool_invocation is still returning key-ring-unreadable in production logs.
findings.evidence: docs/gates/USER-GATE-D.md line 24: '(vi) TF-023D-003 closed. _log_tool_invocation reads the active key_id from docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub (replaced pending_021J placeholder).' The TF-023D-003 code change is complete (tools.py _resolve_audit_key_id reads from the pub file). The criterion could be read as satisfied by code review alone. With no key in the pub file, 'reads the active key_id' produces 'key-ring-unreadable' — not a real key_id. The criterion does not explicitly state that a key must exist.
findings.impact: Minimal in single-operator mode where @jrnb2024 knows the operational state. In multi-operator mode or future audit, criterion (vi) marked checked could be misread as 'key attribution is working' when it is not. Nit severity because the ambiguity is cosmetic and does not change the security posture directly.
findings.mitigation: Tighten criterion (vi) text: 'TF-023D-003 closed (code reads from docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub). AND at least one current=true entry exists in the pub file (key provisioned). Verify: TOOL_LOGGER output shows key_id != key-ring-unreadable in a live MCP session.' This separates the two distinct conditions with explicit verification steps.

self_reported_concerns: MAJ-SAFE-001 (docs/gates/** CODEOWNERS gap) is the only blocking finding. It is a one-line CODEOWNERS fix. In current single-operator mode the gap has no practical exploit path; the window opens at the 2026-07-21 bus-factor-1 review if additional maintainers are added before the line is added. The fix should land in this PR.

MIN-SAFE-003 (TF-023A-002 undelivered) conflicts with the DISPATCH-NOTE scope decision that listed it as IN. If the operator chooses to defer the notification past merge, DISPATCH-NOTE should be updated to reflect OUT-tracked-forward so the scope record is accurate. Merging with the scope record showing IN but delivery absent is a governance inconsistency.

The self-referential OIDC trust model was assessed as sound and bounded. SCP verifying its own emit via OIDC is acceptable because the attestation is issued by GitHub's OIDC provider against a specific job_workflow_ref claim bound to the reusable workflow SHA. SCP controls neither the OIDC token issuance nor the gh attestation verify invocation (that runs in the aggregator's GitHub-hosted runner). The self-reference is a data-flow loop (SCP emits → aggregator aggregates → index consumed by SCP MCP), not a trust loop.

MIN-SAFE-001 and MIN-SAFE-002 both resolve when the operator provisions a key: MIN-SAFE-001's practical risk disappears (the code path that matters is the ValueError path from a populated-but-no-current-key ring, which resolves correctly); MIN-SAFE-002's audit degradation resolves. Tracking both as distinct findings is correct — the code coverage gap (MIN-SAFE-001) and the operational gap (MIN-SAFE-002) have different mitigations.
summary: Slice 023E presents 1 MAJ, 3 MIN, and 1 nit finding under the SAFETY/BYPASS lens. MAJ-SAFE-001: docs/gates/** is absent from CODEOWNERS. The USER-GATE-D Threshold A sign-off artefact (the gate that closes WP-SCP-023) has no code owner. In multi-maintainer mode — triggered by the planned 2026-07-21 bus-factor-1 escalation review — any contributor could fill in the signature stub and merge it without @jrnb2024 approval, falsely closing WP-SCP-023 in the governance record. Fix: add docs/gates/** @jrnb2024 to CODEOWNERS (one line, before the /CODEOWNERS self-protection line per ORDERING INVARIANT). All other core safety properties hold: the SHA pin (5ff2acd7e756ed748cd9466bb1ee30e7e1224eb5) in the wrapper exactly matches the registry expected_scp_workflow_ref; the self-referential OIDC model is bounded by GitHub's token issuer (SCP cannot forge its own attestation); _resolve_audit_key_id fallback never blocks within the covered exception set; _current_signing_key_id is the same function used by propose() signing path; USER-GATE-D is unambiguously not-yet-signed with a blank stub; the aggregator is cron-only and pulls a prior-run artifact — no infinite self-loop is possible; no new bypass surfaces were introduced by the deltas.
